      required phrases present here: []
      text (FULL, untruncated):
<u>The **Fleet Sharing submodule** allows users to create, manage, and monitor fleet sharing records.</u>

* <u>Click on **+ New fleet sharing** for creating new record</u>

* <u>Click **Filters** to access filtering options.</u>

* <u>Search for the required Fleet sharing by selecting the desired **Period** or by entering the subject in</u> <u>the **Search by tittle.**</u>

* <u>Click **Apply** to filter the records or **Clear** to reset the filters.</u>

* <u>Use the action icons to manage the selected Fleet sharing (See Figure 2).</u>
  [4] Audit - Fleet Sharing Manual- Office_R1_30.06.2026 — 3.1 DESCRIPTION (p.6)
      required phrases present here: []
      text (FULL, untruncated):
* <u>Enter the mandatory details, including the **Title** and **Date**.</u>

* <u>Enter the Fleet Sharing **Description** in the description field.</u>

* <u>Upload supporting attachments, if applicable.</u>

* <u>Click **View** to open the uploaded attachments.</u>

* <u>Click **Save** to save the Fleet Sharing record. (*See Figure 3*).</u>

screenshot: Fleet Sharing form interface showing mandatory fields, description box, and upload/save buttons

Figure 3

      required phrases present here: []
      text (FULL, untruncated):
* <u>Enter the required Discussion Date under **Step 2**.</u>

* <u>Click **Submit** to confirm that the Fleet Sharing record has been discussed onboard. (See Figure 3)</u>

[icon: hand pointing right] Once the record is submitted, the **Confirmation** column in the Fleet Sharing overview table is automatically updated for both **Vessel** and **Office** users, indicating that the discussion has been completed.

ANSWER (verbatim):
An office user can delete a Fleet Sharing record **only while it is in Draft status**. Once submitted, it **cannot be deleted**; submitted records also cannot be edited.

**Source:** Fleet Sharing Manual – Office, Figure 2 (p. 5); Section 3.3 Submission (p. 8).

Q: What are the steps to add an action item that vessels need to complete on a fleet sharing record?
EXPECTED manual: Audit - Fleet Sharing Manual- Office_R1_30.06.2026.pdf  pages [6]  section 3.2 ACTIONS
MANUAL EVIDENCE (verified when the case was written): Click + Add Action to create a new action. In the Add Action window, enter the mandatory details marked with (*), including the Nature of Action and Due Date. Click Save to add the action to the Fleet Sharing record.
REQUIRED phrases: ['+ add action', 'nature of action', 'due date']   (in answer: ['+ add action', 'nature of action', 'due date'])
FORBIDDEN phrases: ['edit icon', 'delete icon']   (in answer: [])

CITATIONS SHOWN TO THE USER:
  [1] Audit - Fleet Sharing Manual- Vessel_R1_30.06.2026 — Step 3 – Actions (p.6)
  [2] Audit - Fleet Sharing Manual- Office_R1_30.06.2026 — 3.2 ACTIONS (p.6)  <== expected manual+page
  [3] Audit - Fleet Sharing Manual- Vessel_R1_30.06.2026 — Step 2 – Discussion Record (p.5)
  [4] Audit - Fleet Sharing Manual- Office_R1_30.06.2026 — Document (p.7)
  [5] Audit - Fleet Sharing Manual- Office_R1_30.06.2026 — 4.0 STATUS INDICATOR (p.9)

EXCERPTS ACTUALLY SUPPLIED TO THE MODEL:
  [1] Audit - Fleet Sharing Manual- Vessel_R1_30.06.2026 — Step 3 – Actions (p.6)
      required phrases present here: []
      text (FULL, untruncated):
* Enter the **Date Completed** for the action in the **Update Action** window.

* Upload the required supporting attachments, if applicable.

* Click **Submit** to submit the Fleet Sharing record. (See Figure 4)

☞ After updating the Date Closed for all actions, click **Submit** to submit the record.

☞ The Actions Completed and Date Completed columns in the Fleet Sharing table will be updated accordingly.

screenshot: Actions section of the Fleet Sharing interface showing a table of actions with status icons and callouts for editing, adding comments, and uploading attachments.

Figure 4
  [2] Audit - Fleet Sharing Manual- Office_R1_30.06.2026 — 3.2 ACTIONS (p.6)  <== expected source
      required phrases present here: ['+ add action', 'nature of action', 'due date']
      text (FULL, untruncated):
<u>This section allows users to create and manage actions that are required to be completed by the vessels.</u>

* Click **+ Add Action** to create a new action. (See Figure 4)

 * In the **Add Action window**, enter the mandatory details marked with (**\***), including the Nature of Action and Due Date. (See figure 5)

 * Click **Save** to add the action to the Fleet Sharing record.

 * Repeat the above steps to add additional actions, if required.

* Click the **Edit** icon to modify an existing action.

* Click the **Delete** icon to remove an action.

* Click **Upload** to attach supporting documents related to the action.

* Click **View** to open or delete the uploaded attachments.
 (See Figure 4,5).

* <u>Click **Submit** to confirm that the Fleet Sharing record has been discussed onboard. (See Figure 3)</u>

[icon: hand pointing right] Once the record is submitted, the **Confirmation** column in the Fleet Sharing overview table is automatically updated for both **Vessel** and **Office** users, indicating that the discussion has been completed.

  [5] Audit - Fleet Sharing Manual- Office_R1_30.06.2026 — 4.0 STATUS INDICATOR (p.9)
      required phrases present here: []
      text (FULL, untruncated):
* <u>Click the **List** icon under the **Actions** column to display the vessel-wise action completion status.</u>

* <u>The **Actions Completed** column displays the number of vessels that have completed all assigned actions</u> <u>against the total number of vessels to which the Fleet sharing was shared.</u>

* <u>Review the **Action Completed** and **Date Completed** columns to monitor the action progress for each</u> <u>vessel.</u>

<u>(See Figure 7)</u>

screenshot: Fleet Sharing Audit Dashboard showing vessel-wise action completion status with callouts for tracking responses and expanding details.

Figure 7

<mark>☞ The Actions Completed count is updated automatically as vessels close their assigned actions.</mark>

ANSWER (verbatim):
In the **Office Fleet Sharing interface**:

1. Click **+ Add Action**.
2. In the **Add Action** window, enter all mandatory fields marked with **\***, including **Nature of Action** and **Due Date**.
3. Click **Save** to add the action to the Fleet Sharing record.
4. Repeat these steps for any additional actions.
5. If needed, click **Upload** to attach supporting documents; use **View** to open or delete uploaded attachments.

Source: **Audit – Fleet Sharing Manual – Office_R1_30.06.2026**, section **3.2 ACTIONS**, p. 6–7.

* <u>The **Actions Completed** column displays the number of vessels that have completed all assigned actions</u> <u>against the total number of vessels to which the Fleet sharing was shared.</u>

* <u>Review the **Action Completed** and **Date Completed** columns to monitor the action progress for each</u> <u>vessel.</u>

ANSWER (verbatim):
On the **Office** fleet sharing record:

1. Click **+ Add Action**.
2. In the **Add Action** window, enter all mandatory fields marked with **\***, including **Nature of Action** and **Due Date**.
3. Click **Save** to add the action.
4. Repeat these steps for additional actions, if required.
5. If needed, use **Upload** to attach supporting documents; use **View** to open or delete them.

The Vessel procedure covers completing and submitting assigned actions, not adding them.

**Source:** *Audit - Fleet Sharing Manual- Office_R1_30.06.2026*, §3.2 “ACTIONS,” p.6; Document, p.7.

      text (FULL, untruncated):
* Click on the ‘Admin’ sub-module. (Ref Figure 12)

* Click the ‘Ship’s Certificates’ sub-submodule to view certificate details; the ‘Master’ tab is displayed by default. (Ref Figure 12)

* Upon entering the ‘Ship’s Certificates’ sub-submodule, the system automatically opens the ‘Master’ tab by default, allowing users to view all certificate details:

 * **Master Tab**: The Master tab serves as the central repository for all certificate master records available in the system. It allows administrators to define and maintain certificate types, categories, groups, regulatory references, and certificate labels. This view establishes the standard certificate structure that can be applied across companies and vessels. (Ref Figure 12)

 * **Company Tab**: The Company tab displays certificate records configured for individual companies. It allows administrators to review company-specific certificate requirements, certificate labels, regulatory references, and company group assignments. This view helps ensure that the appropriate certificate masters are assigned and maintained at the company level. (Ref Figure 12)

 * **Vessel Tab**: The Vessel tab displays certificate records applicable

Source: [2] PMS User Manual for Office/Sail Admin, p. 13, Figure 15; [1] Ship-Side Operational Notes, §1.1.13.3.

* Upon entering the ‘Ship’s Certificates’ sub-submodule, the system automatically opens the ‘Master’ tab by default, allowing users to view all certificate details:

 * **Master Tab**: The Master tab serves as the central repository for all certificate master records available in the system. It allows administrators to define and maintain certificate types, categories, groups, regulatory references, and certificate labels. This view establishes the standard certificate structure that can be applied across companies and vessels. (Ref Figure 12)

 * **Company Tab**: The Company tab displays certificate records configured for individual companies. It allows administrators to review company-specific certificate requirements, certificate labels, regulatory references, and company group assignments. This view helps ensure that the appropriate certificate masters are assigned and maintained at the company level. (Ref Figure 12)

 * **Vessel Tab**: The Vessel tab displays certificate records applicable

ANSWER (verbatim):
Yes. The manual states that the procedure for adding attachments and saving finding details also applies to **Positive Observations and LAE finding details**.

1. Select the **VIQ Ref.**; the related TMSA Ref, Initial Risk, Final Risk, and VIQ Question populate automatically.
2. Add the **Ques Category**, **SOC**, and **NOC**.
3. Enter the **Negative observation** and click **Add New**.
4. Click **Upload** to add the required attachments.
5. Click **Save** to save the finding details.
6. Click **Inspection** to return to the Inspection Records page.

For a JSON-file import, the inspection and observation details—including **Positive** and **LAE** findings—are populated automatically and the inspection record is created. Any additional supporting attachments must still be uploaded manually.

Source:  
- Manual entry: *Audit - History Manual_R1_30.06.2026*, sections **2.1.2 Observation Page** (p.8) and **2.1.4 Adding Attachments** (p.10).  
- Positive/LAE applicability: *Audit - History Manual_R1_30.06.2026*, **2.1.4 Adding Attachments** (p.10).  
- JSON import: *Audit - History Manual_R1_30.06.2026*, **Document** (p.13).

Yes. The manual explicitly says to follow the same procedure for adding **Positive Observations and LAE finding details**.

1. Select the **VIQ Ref.**; the related TMSA Ref, Initial Risk, Final Risk, and VIQ Question populate automatically.
2. Add the **Ques Category, SOC, and NOC**.
3. Enter the observation or finding details.
4. Click **Add New**.
5. Click **Upload** to add the required attachments.
6. Click **Save** at the top or bottom of the page.
7. Click **Inspection** to return to the Inspection Records page.

A separate supported route is to upload a JSON file: the inspection and observation details—including Positive and LAE findings—are imported automatically and the inspection record is created. Any additional attachments must still be uploaded manually.

**Source:**  
- Manual entry: *Audit - History Manual_R1_30.06.2026*, sections 2.1.2 “Observation Page” (p.8) and 2.1.4 “Adding Attachments” (p.10).  
- JSON import: *Audit - History Manual_R1_30.06.2026*, “Document” (p.13).

5. The new preparation record is added to the Preparation listing for further actions.
6. An email notification is automatically sent to the **Vessel** when the record is created.

ANSWER (verbatim):
1. On the preparation checklist, select the question and click its **Attachments** (paperclip) icon.
2. Click **Browse** to select a document or image, or drag and drop the file into the upload area. Multiple attachments may be added to the question.
3. Save periodically when uploading multiple or large attachments. Keep the combined size of files in one upload at **20 MB or less**, and the combined size between consecutive saves or Offline-to-Online synchronizations at **150 MB or less**.
4. After uploading, the attachment appears under the corresponding question. You can **view, download, or delete** it by clicking the delete icon.

**Source:** Audit – Preparation Manual_Office_R1_30.06.2026, §§2.3 “Attachment Icon” (p.7), 4.3.4 “Adding Attachment(s)” (p.19), and 4.3.5 “Delete Attachments” (p.21).

* Click '**+ New Preparation**' to create a new preparation record.

* <u>A **Preparation Details** window is displayed. Select the required **Inspection Type**.</u>

* <u>Complete all mandatory preparation details by selecting the appropriate values from</u> <u>the drop-down lists and entering the required information.</u>

* <u>Click **Save Changes** to create the preparation record or **Discard** to cancel without saving.</u>

* <u>The newly created preparation record is added to the Preparation listing and is ready for</u> <u>further actions.</u>

ANSWER (verbatim):
1. Select the checklist question and click its **Attachments** icon.
2. Add the file by clicking **Browse** and selecting it, or by dragging and dropping it into the upload area.
3. Multiple attachments may be added to the question. Keep the combined size of files in one upload at **20 MB or less**.
4. Save periodically, especially when uploading multiple or large files. The combined size of all attachments between two consecutive **Save** actions or Offline-to-Online synchronizations should not exceed **150 MB**.
5. After uploading, the attachment appears under the corresponding question in the **Uploaded** section. You can **view** or **download** it.
6. To remove it, click its **delete** icon.

**Source:** Audit – Preparation Manual_Office_R1_30.06.2026, sections 2.3 “Attachment Icon” (p.7), 4.3.4 “Adding Attachment(s)” (p.19), and 4.3.5 “Delete Attachments” (p.21).

ANSWER (verbatim):
No. A vessel user must not fill in the Office Closeout comments or close the incident report.

1. Complete all vessel actions. The report remains open and requires closure by the office.
2. An office user reviews the report, adds Office Comments if needed, records the closure details, and submits/closes the report.
3. Vessel users should not enter or modify information in the Office Closeout section.

**Source:** Office closeout — *Incident User Manual*, Part K: Office Closeout, p.18; *Near Miss User Manual*, §6 Office Closeout, p.11. Pending office closure — *Incident User Manual*, p.19.

* Users can add **Sequence of Events** details using either of the following methods:

 * <u>**METHOD 1</u>:** Enter or paste the details directly into the editor box.

 * <u>**METHOD 2</u>:** Use the **Date / Time / Description** section to enter details of sequence of events.

 *(See Figure 8)*

  [2] Incident - Incident User Manual R0_20.05.2026 — ⮚ METHOD 2: (p.9)  <== expected source
      required phrases present here: ['date, time, and description', 'new date', 'key moment']
      text (FULL, untruncated):
1. Enter the sequence of event details using the **Date, Time, and Description fields.**

2. Click the **'+' icon** to add additional event entries for the same date.

3. Click **'New Date'** to add event entries for a different or consecutive date.

4. Select the **Key Moment** checkbox to highlight important events, if applicable.

5. Click the **'Bin' icon** to remove an event entry, if required.

6. Click **Save** to store the Part D details.

*(See Figure 9)*

ANSWER (verbatim):
The second way is to use the **Date / Time / Description** fields:

1. Enter the event details in the **Date, Time, and Description** fields.
2. Click **“+”** to add more events for the same date.
3. Click **“New Date”** to add events for a different or consecutive date.
4. Select **Key Moment** to highlight an important event, if applicable.
5. Click the **Bin** icon to remove an event entry, if needed.
6. Click **Save** to store the Part D details.

**Source:** Incident User Manual R0_20.05.2026, Part D: Sequence of Events, “METHOD 2,” p. 9.

ANSWER (verbatim):

ANSWER (verbatim):
No. A promotion review form does not appear directly in the **Promotion** sub-module.

1. In the **Admin** sub-module, open the promotion form configuration using the **Edit** icon.
2. Enter all required information in **Part A** and **Part B**.
3. Click **Save Form**.
4. The form must be created and released through **Admin**. Only then can it be filled in from the **Promotion** sub-module.

After opening **Promotions**, the system initially displays the **All** sub-submodule.

**Source:** Crewing User Manual R2_10.06.2026, “Document,” p.100; “How to Execute a Promotion,” §1.6.1.5, p.48; “How to Access Promotions,” §1.6.1.1, p.45.

ANSWER (verbatim):
No. A promotion review form does not appear directly in the Promotion sub-module.

1. In the **Admin** sub-module, the promotion form must first be created and released.
2. Its required information must be entered in **Part A** and **Part B**, then the administrator clicks **Save Form**.
3. After the form is saved, it can be filled in from the **Promotion** sub-module. The **Promotions** sub-module opens the **All** view by default.

ANSWER (verbatim):
Follow the steps in the **In-Progress** sub-sub-module. The Crew Pool form is completed using the same steps as the **“How to Create a New Crew Record”** procedure:

1. Open **In-Progress**.
2. Click **“+ New Crew.”**
3. In the **Recruitment Application – New Candidate** form, click **Edit** to enter the required information.
4. Save the form at any stage with **Save Draft**.
5. Complete the applicable sections and submit when required. Fields marked with a red asterisk are mandatory in the Crew Pool form.

Source: Crewing User Manual, **1.3.1.5 How to Add Records to Crew Pool**, p. 29; **1.2.1.3 How to Create a New Crew Record**, p. 14; **SAIL - Crewing Module User Manual**, p. 16.

The application moves forward to Part B (Office Screening) for crew executive processing.

* Upon submission of Part A, the system automatically redirects to Part B, where the office user can enter the required details. (Ref Figure 14)

* Click on the ‘Comment’ icon to add observations or notes. (Ref Figure 14)

* Click the ‘Submit’ button to save each section of the form. (Ref Figure 14)

screenshot_from_computer: Recruitment Application - Test interface showi

ANSWER (verbatim):
Follow the steps in the **In-Progress** sub-sub-module. The Crew Pool form uses the same steps as the **“How to Create a New Crew Record”** section.

1. Go to **In-Progress**.
2. Click **“+ New Crew.”**
3. Complete the **Recruitment Application – New Candidate** form:
   - Part A: applicant
   - Part B: company application processing
   - Part C: company approval process
4. Click the **Edit** icon to enter information; fields are read-only by default.
5. Use **Save Draft** to save the form at any stage.
6. Fields marked with a red asterisk (*) in the Crew Pool form are mandatory.

Source:  
- Crew Pool — “How to Add Records to Crew Pool,” §1.3.1.5, p.29.  
- New Crew Record — “How to Create a New Crew Record,” §1.2.1.3, p.14.

ANSWER (verbatim):
Clicking the **eye icon** differs by version:

1. **Office:** For the selected MoC record, it lets users **view, edit, or export** the record.
2. **Vessel:** It lets users **view the documents attached** to the selected MoC record.

So, the icon is not described identically: Office uses it for record viewing, editing, and exporting, while Vessel uses it for viewing attachments.

**Source:** Office MoC User Manual, “MoC Log – Overview,” p. 7; Vessel MoC User Manual, “MoC Log – Overview,” p. 5.

1. **Office RA** — after saving the RA form, it is stored in the **Office RA sub-module**.
2. **Vessel RA** — after saving, it is stored in the **Vessels RA sub-module**.

Click **Back** on the RA form to return to the MoC form. The destination depends on which RA option you selected.

  [2] Safety - MOC User Manual_Office_R0_31.03.2026 — PART – C (Continued) (p.13)  <== expected source
      required phrases present here: ['ra sub-module', 'ra form']
      text (FULL, untruncated):
* To add any additional **Implication**, click on the **"+Add Implication"** icon.

* Proceed to **Section C3 – Risk Assessment**, where you can either upload an existing RA using the **Upload** icon or link a new RA using the **Link** icon.

* After clicking the Link icon, select either Office RA or Vessel RA as applicable.
 *(See Figure 12)*

☞ **Note:** Any additional implication can be deleted using the **Delete** icon.
All actions linked to that implication will also be deleted.
After deletion, review the **Part E – Action table** to ensure data consistency.

☞ **Note:** After selecting the relevant **RA option**, the user will be redirected to the **RA form**.
Once the details are saved, the RA will be stored in the appropriate **RA sub-module**.
Click the **Back** icon on the RA form to return to the MoC form.

screenshot: MoC form interface showing Section C3 Risk Assessment with callouts for adding implications and linking RAs

  [3] Safety - Risk Assessment User Manual_Office_R1_30.05.2026 — 6.6 COMPLETING OFFICE RA - PART C (CHECKOUT) (p.16)
      required phrases present here: []
      text (FULL, untruncated):
* All actions added in *Part- B* are displayed under **"C.3 Action Status"**

I. Fill in all required details in **Part C** as applicable.

II. Use **Edit** icon to modify or edit a particular action or **Delete** icon to remove it.

III. Enter **RA Approval** information as per company requirements by selecting the **Level, Status, Approval Date**, and **Approver** details accordingly.

IV. Click **Submit** to save *Part C* information.

(See Figure 21)

  [4] Safety - Risk Assessment User Manual_Office_R1_30.05.2026 — 6.1 HOW TO CREATE A OFFICE RISK ASSESSMENT (p.11)

      text (FULL, untruncated):
* In the Office RA section, click on ‘**+ New RA**’ button to create new Office Risk Assessment. (See Figure 11)

screenshot: Risk Assessment interface showing the Office Risk Assessment section with a callout pointing to the + New RA button

<u>Figure 11</u>

☞ New Risk Assessment can be created in three ways: (See Figure 12)

* Import from the ‘**Generic Library.**’

* Import an existing Risk Assessment from the ‘**Office Library.**’

* Create a fresh Risk Assessment by clicking ‘**Create Fresh RA**’

screenshot: Office Risk Assessment list with a pop-up window titled New Risk Assessment showing three options: Generic Library, Office Library, and Create Fresh RA

<u>Figure 12</u>
  [5] Safety - Risk Assessment User Manual_Office_R1_30.05.2026 — 3. NAVIGATING THE RISK ASSESSMENT SUB-MODULE (p.6)
      required phrases present here: []
      text (FULL, untruncated):
* The Risk Assessment sub-module is divided into the following sections, accessible from the left sidebar:

 * **Generic RA Library** – View and manage the generic Risk Assessment library.

 * **Office RA** – Create and manage office Risk Assessments.

 * **Vessels RA** – View and manage vessel-specific Risk Assessments.

 * **Key Personnel** – Manage personnel involved in the Risk Assessment approval process.

(See Figure 5)

screenshot: Risk Assessment sub-module interface showing Generic RA Library with a list of risk assessments and a sidebar for navigation.

<u>Figure 5</u>

<mark>icon: hand pointer The selected section in the sidebar is highlighted to indicate the active section.</mark>

ANSWER (verbatim):
After clicking **Link** in Section C3:

1. Select **Office RA** or **Vessel RA**, as applicable.
2. Complete the redirected RA form and save it.
3. The RA is stored in the corresponding sub-module:
   - **Office RA** → **Office RA** sub-module.
   - **Vessel RA** → **Vessels RA** sub-module.
4. Click **Back** on the RA form to return to the MoC form.

Source: *Safety - MOC User Manual_Office_R0_31.03.2026*, Part C (Continued), p.13; *Safety - Risk Assessment User Manual_Office_R1_30.05.2026*, section 3, p.6.

CASE moc-vessel-2 [procedure] run 1   stored verdict: answer=True citation=True support=not captured
Q: What are the steps to fill out and submit Part A of a Vessel MoC form?

☞ The approval workflow for Generic Risk Assessment (GRA), Office Risk Assessments (Office RA) and Vessel Risk Assessments (VRA) can be configured in accordance with the company’s procedures.

☞ The approval hierarchy for GRA, Office RA and VRA is configurable up to **Level 4**.

☞ The **Approval Levels** displayed in the drop-down list are based on the approval hierarchy configured for the client.

☞ For Vessel Risk Assessments (VRA), the applicable approval level can be defined separately for each Risk Assessment type in line with the Company’s approval procedures.

ANSWER (verbatim):
No. A Position/Rank can be assigned only **one Approval Level** for Risk Assessments.

If the Position/Rank needs a different Approval Level:

1. Edit the existing approver record.
2. Change its Approval Level.
3. Do not create a second approver record for the same Position/Rank.

This applies to the approval hierarchy for Generic RA, Office RA, and Vessel RA.

**Source:** Safety – Risk Assessment User Manual_Office_R1_30.05.2026, “Key Personnel – Managing Approvers,” p. 25.

EXPECTED manual: Safety - Risk Assessment User Manual_Office_R1_30.05.2026.pdf  pages [7]  section 4. HOW TO APPLY FILTERS

The available filter options vary depending on the selected section. The example below demonstrates the filtering process in the Office RA section.

☞ The filtering functionality is same across the **Generic RA Library**, **Office RA**, and **Vessels RA** sections.

☞ The available filter options vary depending on the selected section.

☞ The example below demonstrates the filtering process in the Office RA section.

* In the Office RA section, click the **Filters** button to display the available filtering options.

* Select the required filter options:

 * **Period** – Filter records by time-period.

 * **Department** – Display Risk Assessments for a specific department.

 * **RA Type** – Filter records by the selected RA type.

 * **Search** – Enter keywords to search by Report ID or RA Name.

* Click **Apply** to display the filtered results.

* Click **Clear** to remove all selected filters and display the complete list of Risk Assessments.

(See Figure 6)

      required phrases present here: []

* Click on the **‘Filters’** tab to see filtering options.

* Select the required filters to view reports based on the desired **time period, group, sub-group, vessel type,** and **RA type.**

* Click **‘Apply’** to filter the results or **‘Clear’** to reset the selection.
 (See Figure 5)

* Click on the **‘Eye’** icon to view the ‘Risk Assessment’ form. *(See Figure 7)*

screenshot: Risk Assessment table showing an eye icon highlighted with a callout 'Click to view GRA form'

icon: hand pointing right The **GRA Library** is available to vessel users for **viewing purposes only**.

ANSWER (verbatim):
The filters work the same way across the **Generic RA Library, Office RA, and Vessel RA** sections. They are illustrated separately, but the filtering process is shared. The available filter fields vary by section.

1. Open **Filters** (or the **Filters** tab).
2. Select the required filters:
   - **Office RA:** Period, Department, RA Type, or Search by Report ID/RA Name.
   - **Generic/Vessel RA:** Time period, group, sub-group, vessel type, or RA type.
3. Click **Apply** to display the filtered results.
4. Click **Clear** to remove the selections and show the complete list.

The Vessel manual specifically states that filtering is the same for **Generic Risk Assessment (GRA)** and **Vessel Risk Assessment (VRA)**. The GRA Library is available to vessel users for viewing only.

**Source:**  
- Safety – Risk Assessment User Manual_Office_R1_30.05.2026, §4 “How to Apply Filters,” p.7.  
- Safety – Risk Assessment User Manual_Vessel_R1_30.05.2026, §3 “How to Apply Filters,” p.6.

ANSWER (verbatim):
To start a brand-new Vessel Risk Assessment:

1. Go to the **Vessel RA** tab.
2. Click **+ New RA**.
3. Choose one of these three options:
   - Import from the **Generic Library**.
   - Import an existing Risk Assessment from the **Vessel Library**.
   - Click **Create Fresh RA** to create one from scratch.

**Source:** Generic Library import — *Safety - Risk Assessment User Manual_Office*, §7.1, p.18; *Safety - Risk Assessment User Manual_Vessel*, §6, p.10. Vessel Library import — same sections. Create Fresh RA — same sections.

  [5] Safety - SMS User Manual_Office_R0_31.01.2026 — 3.2 DASHBOARD (p.12)
      required phrases present here: []
      text (FULL, untruncated):
* SMS change request forms can be viewed from the Dashboard.

* Dashboard is divided into two sections: *New Document* and *New Revision*.

 * **New Document** – Displays the record of change requests for documents uploaded in SAIL for the first time.

 * **New Revision** – Displays the record of change requests for revisions uploaded to existing documents.

* Each section includes the following stages:

 * **Draft** – Contains change request forms that are in the proposal stage and have not yet been submitted for approval.

 * **Pending for Approval** – Displays forms that have been submitted for approval but are not yet approved.

 * **Approved** – Displays forms that have been approved by the approver but are not yet released.

 * **Rejected** – Displays forms that have been rejected by the approver.

 * **Released** – The final stage; displays forms that have been released for vessel and office use.

screenshot: SAIL SMS Dashboard interface showing Draft, Pending Approval, Approved, and Released columns with callout boxes explaining the toggle switch and how to view request details.

Figure 17

The steps for approving a revision in **Section 4.2.2** are not included in the provided Safety documentation. The excerpt only gives approval steps for **Section 4.1.2**.

**Source:** Safety - SMS User Manual_Office_R0_31.01.2026, Section 4.1.2, p.17.

      text (FULL, untruncated):
* SMS change request forms can be viewed from the Dashboard.

* Dashboard is divided into two sections: *New Document* and *New Revision*.

 * **New Document** – Displays the record of change requests for documents uploaded in SAIL for the first time.

 * **New Revision** – Displays the record of change requests for revisions uploaded to existing documents.

* Each section includes the following stages:

 * **Draft** – Contains change request forms that are in the proposal stage and have not yet been submitted for approval.

 * **Pending for Approval** – Displays forms that have been submitted for approval but are not yet approved.

 * **Approved** – Displays forms that have been approved by the approver but are not yet released.

 * **Rejected** – Displays forms that have been rejected by the approver.

 * **Released** – The final stage; displays forms that have been released for vessel and office use.

screenshot: SAIL SMS Dashboard interface showing Draft, Pending Approval, Approved, and Released columns with callout boxes explaining the toggle switch and how to view request details.

Figure 17

ANSWER (verbatim):
Section 4.2.2 is not included in the excerpts, so the specific approval procedure for an already-uploaded revision is **not covered in the Safety documentation provided**.

The general approval instructions state that the Approver should:

1. Select **Need Improvement**, **Approved**, or **Rejected**.
2. Enter the **Approval Date** and select the **Username**.
3. Click **Submit** to forward the documents to the releasing authority for release to vessel or office users.

Source:  
- *Safety - SMS User Manual_Office_R0_31.01.2026*, Section 4.1.2 “Approval,” p. 17.

      text (FULL, untruncated):
**Introduction**

* The ‘**Ship’s Certificates**’ sub-submodule is used to manage the master list of certificate types maintained within the system. It enables authorized users to create, configure, and maintain certificate definitions, including certificate names, categories, groups, regulatory references, and applicability settings. The module also allows administrators to control the assignment of certificates at the company and vessel levels, ensuring that certificate requirements are standardized and consistently applied across the fleet.
  [5] Technical - Cert. & Surveys User Manual For Office_Sail Admin_R2_08.06.2026 — 1.2.1.1 HOW TO ACCESS THE SHIP’S CERTIFICATES (p.13)
      required phrases present here: []
      text (FULL, untruncated):
* Click on the ‘Admin’ sub-module. (Ref Figure 12)

* Click the ‘Ship’s Certificates’ sub-submodule to view certificate details; the ‘Master’ tab is displayed by default. (Ref Figure 12)

* Upon entering the ‘Ship’s Certificates’ sub-submodule, the system automatically opens the ‘Master’ tab by default, allowing users to view all certificate details:

 * **Master Tab**: The Master tab serves as the central repository for all certificate master records available in the system. It allows administrators to define and maintain certificate types, categories, groups, regulatory references, and certificate labels. This view establishes the standard certificate structure that can be applied across companies and vessels. (Ref Figure 12)

 * **Company Tab**: The Company tab displays certificate records configured for individual companies. It allows administrators to review company-specific certificate requirements, certificate labels, regulatory references, and company group assignments. This view helps ensure that the appropriate certificate masters are assigned and maintained at the company level. (Ref Figure 12)

 * **Vessel Tab**: The Vessel tab displays certificate records applicable

ANSWER (verbatim):
For an authorized Office user:

1. Click the **Admin** sub-module.
2. Click **Ship’s Certificates**. The **Master** tab opens by default.
3. Click **Edit**.
4. Click **New**. The system adds an editable row at the bottom with an auto-generated **Master ID**.
5. Enter the required details: **Certificate Name, Category, Group, Requirement/Reference, Applicable to Company,** and **Certificate Label**. Mandatory fields must be completed.
6. Click the **Save** icon.
7. Choose **Yes, Reorder** to move the certificate to the selected Category and Group, or **No, Keep at End** to leave it at the end of the table.

The Master list contains system-defined certificates that users cannot delete.

**Source:** Technical - Cert. & Surveys User Manual For Office_Sail Admin_R2_08.06.2026, sections 1.2.1.1 “How to Access the Ship’s Certificates” (p.13), 1.2.1.4 “How to Add a New Master Certificate” (p.17), and technical user manual steps (p.18).

ANSWER (verbatim):
In **Office Sail Admin**, an authorized user can add a new certificate type to the **Master** list as follows:

1. Open the **Admin** sub-module.
2. Open **Ship’s Certificates**. The **Master** tab opens by default.
3. Click **Edit**.
4. Click **New**.
5. In the new editable row, enter the mandatory details:
   - Certificate Name
   - Category
   - Group
   - Requirement/Reference
   - Applicable to Company
   - Certificate Label
6. Click the **Save** icon.
7. Choose **Yes, Reorder** to move the certificate into the selected Category and Group section, or **No, Keep at End** to leave it at the end of the table.

The system automatically generates the new **Master ID**.

ANSWER (verbatim):

3. Click **Save**. The record cannot be saved while any mandatory `*` field is blank.
4. Choose **Yes, Reorder** or **No, Keep at End**.

* Click on the ‘Admin’ sub-module. (Ref Figure 12)

* Click the ‘Ship’s Certificates’ sub-submodule to view certificate details; the ‘Master’ tab is displayed by default. (Ref Figure 12)

* Upon entering the ‘Ship’s Certificates’ sub-submodule, the system automatically opens the ‘Master’ tab by default, allowing users to view all certificate details:

 * **Master Tab**: The Master tab serves as the central repository for all certificate master records available in the system. It allows administrators to define and maintain certificate types, categories, groups, regulatory references, and certificate labels. This view establishes the standard certificate structure that can be applied across companies and vessels. (Ref Figure 12)

 * **Company Tab**: The Company tab displays certificate records configured for individual companies. It allows administrators to review company-specific certificate requirements, certificate labels, regulatory references, and company group assignments. This view helps ensure that the appropriate certificate masters are assigned and maintained at the company level. (Ref Figure 12)

 * **Vessel Tab**: The Vessel tab displays certificate records applicable

ANSWER (verbatim):
The process for a survey record is the same as for a certificate record (section 1.1.3.5, p. 9):

1. Select the required vessel from the **Vessel** dropdown.
2. Click the **Attachment** icon in the survey table’s **Actions** column.
3. In the attachment window, click the upload area and select a **PDF, JPG, or PNG** file.
4. Use **View** to preview an attachment or **Delete** to remove it.
5. Click **Done** to save the changes.

Each attachment can be no larger than **5 MB**. Larger files or unsupported file types cannot be uploaded. If the survey is not listed for the vessel, its corresponding master entry is not marked **Applicable** for that vessel in the Admin sub-module.

**Source:**  
- Technical – Cert. & Surveys User Manual For Office_Sail Admin_R2_08.06.2026, section 1.1.4.5, p. 11, cross-referenced to the same steps in section 1.1.3.5, p. 9.

ANSWER (verbatim):
The survey-specific procedure is **not covered** in the Technical documentation. It only says to refer to the Certificates sub-sub-module; this does not establish whether the survey process is identical or different.

The documented certificate attachment process is:

1. Select the vessel from the **Vessel** dropdown.
2. Click the **Attachment** icon for the certificate record.
3. Click the upload area and select a **PDF, JPG, or PNG** file.
4. Use **View** to preview or **Delete** to remove an attachment.
5. Click **Done** to save the changes.
6. Each attachment must be no larger than **5 MB**. Larger or unsupported files cannot be uploaded.
7. If the survey record is unavailable under **Surveys**, its master entry is not marked **Applicable** for that vessel in the Admin sub-module.

**Source:** Certificates attachment procedure — *Technical - Cert. & Surveys User Manual For Office_Sail Admin_R2_08.06.2026*, §1.1.3.5, p.9; survey attachment note — §1.1.4.5, p.11.

* Click on the ‘Admin’ sub-module. (Ref Figure 12)

* Click the ‘Ship’s Certificates’ sub-submodule to view certificate details; the ‘Master’ tab is displayed by default. (Ref Figure 12)

* Upon entering the ‘Ship’s Certificates’ sub-submodule, the system automatically opens the ‘Master’ tab by default, allowing users to view all certificate details:

 * **Master Tab**: The Master tab serves as the central repository for all certificate master records available in the system. It allows administrators to define and maintain certificate types, categories, groups, regulatory references, and certificate labels. This view establishes the standard certificate structure that can be applied across companies and vessels. (Ref Figure 12)

 * **Company Tab**: The Company tab displays certificate records configured for individual companies. It allows administrators to review company-specific certificate requirements, certificate labels, regulatory references, and company group assignments. This view helps ensure that the appropriate certificate masters are assigned and maintained at the company level. (Ref Figure 12)

 * **Vessel Tab**: The Vessel tab displays certificate records applicable

ANSWER (verbatim):
The manual does not describe a separate survey-attachment workflow. It directs you to the **Certificates** sub-sub-module and says to follow the same steps:

1. Select the vessel from the **Vessel** dropdown.
2. In the survey table, click the **Attachment** icon for the survey record.
3. In the attachment window, click the upload area and select a **PDF, JPG, or PNG** file.
4. Use **View** to preview or **Delete** to remove an attachment.
5. Click **Done** to save the changes.

Each attachment must be **no larger than 5 MB**. If the survey is not listed for the vessel, its master entry is not marked **Applicable** for that vessel in the Admin sub-module. No other difference from certificate attachments is stated.

**Source:**  
- Survey attachments: *Technical - Cert. & Surveys User Manual For Office_Sail Admin_R2_08.06.2026*, §1.1.4.5, p.11.  
- Attachment steps and limits: same manual, §1.1.3.5, p.9.

      required phrases present here: ['current period', 'past their due date']
      text (FULL, untruncated):
* Click the 'Work Orders' sub-module to view all the work orders. (Ref Figure 32)

* Click the required status tab (Scheduled, Due, Overdue, Postponed, Unplanned, Pending Approval, and Completed) to view the corresponding work orders' status. (Ref Figure 32)

screenshot: Work Orders (W\.O) interface showing navigation and status tabs with instructional callouts.

<a id="figure-32"></a>Figure 32

* [icon: hand pointing right] **Scheduled:** Jobs that have been planned and have a future due date.
* **Due:** Jobs that are due within the current period.
* **Overdue:** Jobs past their due date that have not been completed.
* **Postponed:** Jobs that have been deferred with an approved justification.
* **Unplanned:** Details of unplanned work orders will be displayed in this section.

ANSWER (verbatim):
No. A spare part’s ROB cannot be modified unless a storage location is selected first.

1. **Inventory transaction**
   1. Open **Spares > Inventory**.
   2. Click the **Location** icon for the spare part.
   3. Select a location, or click **+ Create New Location**.
   4. Click **Save** to update the ROB.  
   Consumption cannot exceed the current ROB, and updates are recorded in **History**. This applies to the vessel and Office procedures.

2. **Update by location**
   1. Open the **Location** tab.
   2. Select a location from the **Location tree**.
   3. Click the **Loc ROB** value.
   4. Click **Save**.  

**Source:**  
- Vessel Specific Technical User Manual, §1.1.7.2, p.38 — Inventory transactions.  
- Office Sail Admin Technical User Manual, p.45 — Inventory transactions.  
- Vessel Specific Technical User Manual, §1.1.7.3, p.39 — Update spares by location.

  [5] Technical - KB pilot: How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order.md — How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order

      text (FULL, untruncated):
Provenance note: draft code-derived guidance, not a published manual. 3 statement(s) come from the June PMS manuals; 7 statement(s) about roles, switches and automatic generation were inspected in the Technical application code at repository revision cf5241ad6, which the application owner has confirmed is the code running in the Technical application. Where this guidance and a manual differ, say which source says what.
Applies to: Both
Who can do it (role): Depends on the way — (1) planned: nobody, the ship system creates them; office 'Generate Now': Sail Admin only; (2) per-job 'Generate WO': no role check; (3) unplanned: no role check. Normal sign-in and vessel access apply to all.
Prerequisites (switches, settings, job/component state): Office 'Generate Now' and office per-job 'Generate WO' both need the vessel's 'office work-order generation' switch ON (off by default, set by a Sail Admin on 'Lead Time & Grace Period Settings'). Unplanned needs no switch. A job with an active work order cannot get another one.
Steps:
1. Planned (scheduled) work orders — generated by the system from each job's frequency and next due date. ON THE SHIP: automatic, once a day, no user action. IN THE OFFICE: nothing runs automatically; a Sail Admin can click 'Generate Now' on the Work Orders screen for one vessel, only if that vessel's switch is on. Details: planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md and office-generate-now.md.
2. One job on demand — Components → (Office: select the vessel) → open the component → Part C → 'Generate WO' → choose the reason (Planning / Breakdown / Other). No role check on this path (sign-in and vessel access still apply); in the office only if the vessel switch is on; the job must be active and must not already have an active work order. Details: office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
3. Unplanned work — Work Orders → (Office: select the vessel) → '+ Unplanned W.O' → Part A, Save → Part B, Submit Work Order. No role check on this path, no switch. Details: unplanned-wo.md.
Exceptions / edge cases: The Sail Admin requirement belongs to 'Generate Now' only; it does not apply to per-job 'Generate WO' or to unplanned work orders.
Where the manual differs: The June manuals describe only ways 2 and 3 and state no office conditions; automatic ship generation and 'Generate Now' are absent from them. See CONFLICTS.md.
Related procedures: planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md · office-generate-now.md · office-generate-wo-per-job.md · unplanned-wo.md

ANSWER (verbatim):
Yes. For a **locked work order**, approval is permitted only after:

1. The **Tech Superintendent acknowledges** it.
2. The **HOD approves** it afterward.

This restriction is stated for both vessel and office approval workflows.

**Source:**  
- Vessel Specific PMS User Manual, §1.1.5.7, p.30  
- Office Sail Admin PMS User Manual, §1.1.5.7, p.34

Provenance note: draft code-derived guidance, not a published manual. 3 statement(s) come from the June PMS manuals; 7 statement(s) about roles, switches and automatic generation were inspected in the Technical application code at repository revision cf5241ad6, which the application owner has confirmed is the code running in the Technical application. Where this guidance and a manual differ, say which source says what.
Applies to: Both
Who can do it (role): Depends on the way — (1) planned: nobody, the ship system creates them; office 'Generate Now': Sail Admin only; (2) per-job 'Generate WO': no role check; (3) unplanned: no role check. Normal sign-in and vessel access apply to all.
Prerequisites (switches, settings, job/component state): Office 'Generate Now' and office per-job 'Generate WO' both need the vessel's 'office work-order generation' switch ON (off by default, set by a Sail Admin on 'Lead Time & Grace Period Settings'). Unplanned needs no switch. A job with an active work order cannot get another one.
Steps:
1. Planned (scheduled) work orders — generated by the system from each job's frequency and next due date. ON THE SHIP: automatic, once a day, no user action. IN THE OFFICE: nothing runs automatically; a Sail Admin can click 'Generate Now' on the Work Orders screen for one vessel, only if that vessel's switch is on. Details: planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md and office-generate-now.md.
2. One job on demand — Components → (Office: select the vessel) → open the component → Part C → 'Generate WO' → choose the reason (Planning / Breakdown / Other). No role check on this path (sign-in and vessel access still apply); in the office only if the vessel switch is on; the job must be active and must not already have an active work order. Details: office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
3. Unplanned work — Work Orders → (Office: select the vessel) → '+ Unplanned W.O' → Part A, Save → Part B, Submit Work Order. No role check on this path, no switch. Details: unplanned-wo.md.
Exceptions / edge cases: The Sail Admin requirement belongs to 'Generate Now' only; it does not apply to per-job 'Generate WO' or to unplanned work orders.
Where the manual differs: The June manuals describe only ways 2 and 3 and state no office conditions; automatic ship generation and 'Generate Now' are absent from them. See CONFLICTS.md.
Related procedures: planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md · office-generate-now.md · office-generate-wo-per-job.md · unplanned-wo.md

ANSWER (verbatim):
Yes. For a locked work order, approval is permitted only after:

1. Tech Superintendent acknowledgement.
2. HOD approval.

This restriction is stated for both Ship and Office approval workflows.

**Source:**  
- *PMS User Manual_Vessel Specific*, §1.1.5.7, p.30.  
- *PMS User Manual For Office_Sail Admin*, §1.1.5.7, p.34.

ANSWER (verbatim):
On the **Office PMS Dashboard**, you can filter by:

1. Click **Filter**.
2. Select **Vessel**, **Scope**, and **Criticality**.
3. Click **Clear** to reset the filters.
4. For an office user, selecting **My Vessel** under Scope displays only vessels assigned to that user.

The excerpts do **not** document the PMS Dashboard on the vessel side, so they do not establish that the vessel side has the same filter set. The vessel-specific manual documents filters in the **Reports** section instead:

1. Use **Search** to find components.
2. Select a **Period**—Year, Quarter, Month, or Date Range—and click **Apply**.
3. Select a department from **All Departments**.

Thus, the documented vessel-side Reports filters are **Search, Period, and All Departments**, not the Dashboard’s **Vessel, Scope, and Criticality** set. Whether the vessel-side Dashboard has the same filters is not covered in the Technical documentation.

**Source:** Office Sail Admin Technical PMS User Manual, §1.1.3.2 “How to Use Filter,” p. 9; Vessel-Specific Technical PMS User Manual, §1.1.9.3 “How to Apply Filter,” p. 46.

ANSWER (verbatim):
On the **PMS Dashboard**, you can filter by:

1. Click **Filter**.
2. Select **Vessel**, **Scope**, and **Criticality**.
3. Click **Clear** to reset the filters.
4. For an office user, selecting **My Vessel** under Scope shows only vessels assigned to that user.

On the **vessel side Reports interface**, the available filters are different:

1. Use **Search** to locate components.
2. Select a **Period**—Year, Quarter, Month, or Date Range—and click **Apply**.
3. Select a **Department** from **All Departments**.

Therefore, the vessel-side set is **not the same** as the PMS Dashboard set: the Dashboard has **Vessel, Scope, and Criticality**, while the vessel Reports interface has **Search, Period, and Department**.

**Source:**  
- PMS User Manual For Office, §1.1.3.2 “How to Use Filter,” p. 9 — Dashboard filters.  
- PMS User Manual—Vessel Specific, §1.1.9.3 “How to Apply Filter,” p. 46 — vessel Reports filters.

ANSWER (verbatim):
For **Stores**, the manuals show a separate entry path, but direct you to the Spares bulk-update procedure for the remaining steps.

1. **Stores bulk update — Vessel**
   1. Open the **Store** sub-sub-module.
   2. Click **+ Bulk Updates Store**.
   3. The manual then directs you to the **Spares** sub-sub-module and its procedure. It also says this process applies to **Stores, Lubes, Chemicals, or Others**, and to the **Inventory, Location, or History** tabs.
   
   The vessel documentation does not provide the subsequent transaction-entry steps in the Stores section.

2. **Stores bulk update — Office**
   1. Open the **Store** sub-sub-module.
   2. Click **+ Bulk Updates Store**.
   3. Follow the Spares bulk-update instructions:
      1. Select **Consume** or **Receive**.
      2. Enter the required details and update quantities in the table.
      3. Click **Save Updates**.

So, Stores has a different starting button and sub-module, but the Office documentation directs the remaining process to the Spares bulk-update instructions. The excerpts do not state any role requirement.

The other supported bulk-update process is **Spares**: open **Spares**, click **Bulk Update Spares**, select the transaction mode, enter/update details, and save the updates.

**Source:**  
- Stores bulk update: *Technical - PMS User Manual_Vessel Specific_R3_08.07.2026*, §1.1.8.3, p.43; *Technical - PMS User Manual For Office_Sail Admin_R2_08.06.2026*, §1.1.8.3, p.50.  
- Spares bulk update: *Technical - PMS User Manual_Vessel Specific_R3_08.07.2026*, §1.1.7.6, p.40; *Technical - PMS User Manual For Office_Sail Admin_R2_08.06.2026*, §§1.1.7.8 and Technical User Manual, p.48.

Q: If I try to generate a work order for a component job that already has an active one, what happens?
EXPECTED manual: Technical - PMS User Manual_Vessel Specific_R3_08.07.2026.pdf  pages [16]  section 1.1.4.2 HOW TO VIEW COMPONENT DETAILS
MANUAL EVIDENCE (verified when the case was written): Ensure that there is no active WO for the same selected job, as the system does not allow the generation of duplicate work orders.
REQUIRED phrases: ['no active wo', 'duplicate']   (in answer: ['duplicate'])
FORBIDDEN phrases: ['multiple work orders allowed', 'no restriction']   (in answer: [])

CITATIONS SHOWN TO THE USER:
  [1] Technical - KB pilot: 'Generate WO' for one job — from the Components page.md — 'Generate WO' for one job — from the Components page
  [2] Technical - PMS User Manual For Office_Sail Admin_R2_08.06.2026 — TECHNICAL USER MANUAL (p.18)
  [3] Technical - PMS User Manual_Vessel Specific_R3_08.07.2026 — TECHNICAL USER MANUAL (p.16)  <== expected manual+page
  [4] Technical - KB pilot: Planned work orders — generated automatically by the ship's daily job-due scan.md — Planned work orders — generated automatically by the ship's daily job-due scan

  [1] Technical - KB pilot: 'Generate WO' for one job — from the Components page.md — 'Generate WO' for one job — from the Components page
      required phrases present here: ['duplicate']
      text (FULL, untruncated):
Provenance note: draft code-derived guidance, not a published manual. 11 statement(s) come from the June PMS manuals; 10 statement(s) about roles, switches and automatic generation were inspected in the Technical application code at repository revision cf5241ad6, which the application owner has confirmed is the code running in the Technical application. Where this guidance and a manual differ, say which source says what.
Applies to: Both
Who can do it (role): No role check on this path. The user must still be signed in and have access to the vessel and the Components page (normal authentication and vessel scope apply); beyond that, the route has no role guard, the controller has no role check, and the service checks only the vessel switch (office) or nothing (ship). It is NOT limited to Sail Admin.
Prerequisites (switches, settings, job/component state):
- On the OFFICE instance: the job's vessel must have its 'office work-order generation' switch ON (off by default; enabled per vessel by a Sail Admin on the 'Lead Time & Grace Period Settings' screen). With the switch off the request is refused with "Office work-order generation is not enabled for this vessel."
- On the SHIP instance: no switch and no role check; the two job conditions below still apply.
- On both instances the job must be active.
- On both instances the job must not already have an active work order.
Steps:
1. Open 'Components' (Office: select the vessel first) and open the component in the component tree.
2. In Part C ('C. Jobs') the component's jobs are listed with Task Type, Frequency, Last Done Date and Next Due Date.
3. Click 'Generate WO' in the Actions column of the job's row.
4. In the 'Generate Work Order' pop-up choose the reason: 'Planning - Scheduled ahead of time', 'Breakdown - Emergency repair needed' or 'Other - Custom reason'.
5. The work order is generated and appears on the Work Orders screen.
Exceptions / edge cases:
- Duplicate: if the job already has an active work order, the system refuses to generate another.
- Inactive job: refused with "Cannot generate work orders for an inactive job".
- The Sail Admin requirement of the office 'Generate Now' button does NOT apply here; the two buttons use different server checks. See office-generate-now.md.
Where the manual differs:
- The June manuals present 'Generate WO' as unconditional. On the office instance the vessel switch must be on. Recorded in CONFLICTS.md.
Related procedures: planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md · office-generate-now.md · unplanned-wo.md

  [4] Technical - KB pilot: Planned work orders — generated automatically by the ship's daily job-due scan.md — Planned work orders — generated automatically by the ship's daily job-due scan
      required phrases present here: []
      text (FULL, untruncated):
Provenance note: draft code-derived guidance, not a published manual. 6 statement(s) come from the June PMS manuals; 7 statement(s) about roles, switches and automatic generation were inspected in the Technical application code at repository revision cf5241ad6, which the application owner has confirmed is the code running in the Technical application. Where this guidance and a manual differ, say which source says what.
Applies to: Vessel
Who can do it (role): None — no user action. Planned (scheduled) work orders are created by the ship system itself.
Prerequisites (switches, settings, job/component state):
- The instance must be a ship instance; the scan does not run on the office (shore) instance.
- The job must be active and attached to a component, with a frequency and a next due date (the job schedule shown in Components → Part C).
- The job must not already have an active work order — one active work order per job at a time.
Steps:
1. Nothing to do. The ship system runs the job-due scan once every 24 hours by default (interval configurable through JOB_DUE_SCAN_INTERVAL_MS) and creates a work order for every job that is due.
2. To see the result, open the 'Work Orders' sub-sub-module and use the status tabs: Scheduled (jobs planned with a future due date), Due (due within the current period), Overdue (past due date, not completed).
3. The work-order number is prefixed with the vessel code: <VESSELCODE>-<JOBCODE>-<COMPONENTCODE>-<YEAR>-<NNN>.
Exceptions / edge cases:
- If a job already has an active work order, the scan does not create another one for it.
- A work order can be generated ahead of the scan for one job with 'Generate WO' on the Components page — see office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
- On the office instance no scan runs. Office-side generation is done by a user in one of two ways: 'Generate Now' for a whole vessel (Sail Admin AND the vessel switch) — see office-generate-now.md — or per-job 'Generate WO' from Components (the vessel switch) — see office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
Where the manual differs:
- The June manuals do not describe automatic generation at all. They describe the Scheduled / Due / Overdue tabs and the job frequency / next due date but never say that the system creates the work orders. Recorded in CONFLICTS.md.
Related procedures: office-generate-now.md · office-generate-wo-per-job.md · unplanned-wo.md
  [5] Technical - KB pilot: How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order.md — How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order
      required phrases present here: []
      text (FULL, untruncated):
Provenance note: draft code-derived guidance, not a published manual. 3 statement(s) come from the June PMS manuals; 7 statement(s) about roles, switches and automatic generation were inspected in the Technical application code at repository revision cf5241ad6, which the application owner has confirmed is the code running in the Technical application. Where this guidance and a manual differ, say which source says what.
Applies to: Both
Who can do it (role): Depends on the way — (1) planned: nobody, the ship system creates them; office 'Generate Now': Sail Admin only; (2) per-job 'Generate WO': no role check; (3) unplanned: no role check. Normal sign-in and vessel access apply to all.
Prerequisites (switches, settings, job/component state): Office 'Generate Now' and office per-job 'Generate WO' both need the vessel's 'office work-order generation' switch ON (off by default, set by a Sail Admin on 'Lead Time & Grace Period Settings'). Unplanned needs no switch. A job with an active work order cannot get another one.
Steps:
1. Planned (scheduled) work orders — generated by the system from each job's frequency and next due date. ON THE SHIP: automatic, once a day, no user action. IN THE OFFICE: nothing runs automatically; a Sail Admin can click 'Generate Now' on the Work Orders screen for one vessel, only if that vessel's switch is on. Details: planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md and office-generate-now.md.
2. One job on demand — Components → (Office: select the vessel) → open the component → Part C → 'Generate WO' → choose the reason (Planning / Breakdown / Other). No role check on this path (sign-in and vessel access still apply); in the office only if the vessel switch is on; the job must be active and must not already have an active work order. Details: office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
3. Unplanned work — Work Orders → (Office: select the vessel) → '+ Unplanned W.O' → Part A, Save → Part B, Submit Work Order. No role check on this path, no switch. Details: unplanned-wo.md.
Exceptions / edge cases: The Sail Admin requirement belongs to 'Generate Now' only; it does not apply to per-job 'Generate WO' or to unplanned work orders.
Where the manual differs: The June manuals describe only ways 2 and 3 and state no office conditions; automatic ship generation and 'Generate Now' are absent from them. See CONFLICTS.md.
Related procedures: planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md · office-generate-now.md · office-generate-wo-per-job.md · unplanned-wo.md

ANSWER (verbatim):
If the component job already has an active work order, the system refuses the request and does not generate another one. This applies on both Office and Ship instances.

The published Office and Vessel manuals state that duplicate work orders are not allowed. The draft code-derived guidance also confirms this behavior.

Source:
- Draft code-derived guidance, “Generate WO” for one job — from the Components page, prerequisites and duplicate exception.
- PMS User Manual For Office, p. 18.
- PMS User Manual Vessel Specific, p. 16.

Provenance note: draft code-derived guidance, not a published manual. 6 statement(s) come from the June PMS manuals; 7 statement(s) about roles, switches and automatic generation were inspected in the Technical application code at repository revision cf5241ad6, which the application owner has confirmed is the code running in the Technical application. Where this guidance and a manual differ, say which source says what.
Applies to: Vessel
Who can do it (role): None — no user action. Planned (scheduled) work orders are created by the ship system itself.
Prerequisites (switches, settings, job/component state):
- The instance must be a ship instance; the scan does not run on the office (shore) instance.
- The job must be active and attached to a component, with a frequency and a next due date (the job schedule shown in Components → Part C).
- The job must not already have an active work order — one active work order per job at a time.
Steps:
1. Nothing to do. The ship system runs the job-due scan once every 24 hours by default (interval configurable through JOB_DUE_SCAN_INTERVAL_MS) and creates a work order for every job that is due.
2. To see the result, open the 'Work Orders' sub-sub-module and use the status tabs: Scheduled (jobs planned with a future due date), Due (due within the current period), Overdue (past due date, not completed).
3. The work-order number is prefixed with the vessel code: <VESSELCODE>-<JOBCODE>-<COMPONENTCODE>-<YEAR>-<NNN>.
Exceptions / edge cases:
- If a job already has an active work order, the scan does not create another one for it.
- A work order can be generated ahead of the scan for one job with 'Generate WO' on the Components page — see office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
- On the office instance no scan runs. Office-side generation is done by a user in one of two ways: 'Generate Now' for a whole vessel (Sail Admin AND the vessel switch) — see office-generate-now.md — or per-job 'Generate WO' from Components (the vessel switch) — see office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
Where the manual differs:
- The June manuals do not describe automatic generation at all. They describe the Scheduled / Due / Overdue tabs and the job frequency / next due date but never say that the system creates the work orders. Recorded in CONFLICTS.md.
Related procedures: office-generate-now.md · office-generate-wo-per-job.md · unplanned-wo.md

Provenance note: draft code-derived guidance, not a published manual. 3 statement(s) come from the June PMS manuals; 7 statement(s) about roles, switches and automatic generation were inspected in the Technical application code at repository revision cf5241ad6, which the application owner has confirmed is the code running in the Technical application. Where this guidance and a manual differ, say which source says what.
Applies to: Both
Who can do it (role): Depends on the way — (1) planned: nobody, the ship system creates them; office 'Generate Now': Sail Admin only; (2) per-job 'Generate WO': no role check; (3) unplanned: no role check. Normal sign-in and vessel access apply to all.
Prerequisites (switches, settings, job/component state): Office 'Generate Now' and office per-job 'Generate WO' both need the vessel's 'office work-order generation' switch ON (off by default, set by a Sail Admin on 'Lead Time & Grace Period Settings'). Unplanned needs no switch. A job with an active work order cannot get another one.
Steps:
1. Planned (scheduled) work orders — generated by the system from each job's frequency and next due date. ON THE SHIP: automatic, once a day, no user action. IN THE OFFICE: nothing runs automatically; a Sail Admin can click 'Generate Now' on the Work Orders screen for one vessel, only if that vessel's switch is on. Details: planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md and office-generate-now.md.
2. One job on demand — Components → (Office: select the vessel) → open the component → Part C → 'Generate WO' → choose the reason (Planning / Breakdown / Other). No role check on this path (sign-in and vessel access still apply); in the office only if the vessel switch is on; the job must be active and must not already have an active work order. Details: office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
3. Unplanned work — Work Orders → (Office: select the vessel) → '+ Unplanned W.O' → Part A, Save → Part B, Submit Work Order. No role check on this path, no switch. Details: unplanned-wo.md.
Exceptions / edge cases: The Sail Admin requirement belongs to 'Generate Now' only; it does not apply to per-job 'Generate WO' or to unplanned work orders.
Where the manual differs: The June manuals describe only ways 2 and 3 and state no office conditions; automatic ship generation and 'Generate Now' are absent from them. See CONFLICTS.md.

ANSWER (verbatim):
For the **Components → Part C → Generate WO** action:

1. If the selected job already has an active work order, the system refuses the request.
2. No duplicate work order is generated.

The published manuals state that the system does not allow duplicate work orders. The draft code-derived guidance confirms the same behavior; it does not specify a particular error message for this case.

**Source:** Office Sail Admin Manual, p. 18; Vessel-Specific Manual, p. 16; draft code-derived guidance, “Generate WO” for one job — from the Components page.

Provenance note: draft code-derived guidance, not a published manual. 11 statement(s) come from the June PMS manuals; 10 statement(s) about roles, switches and automatic generation were inspected in the Technical application code at repository revision cf5241ad6, which the application owner has confirmed is the code running in the Technical application. Where this guidance and a manual differ, say which source says what.
Applies to: Both
Who can do it (role): No role check on this path. The user must still be signed in and have access to the vessel and the Components page (normal authentication and vessel scope apply); beyond that, the route has no role guard, the controller has no role check, and the service checks only the vessel switch (office) or nothing (ship). It is NOT limited to Sail Admin.
Prerequisites (switches, settings, job/component state):
- On the OFFICE instance: the job's vessel must have its 'office work-order generation' switch ON (off by default; enabled per vessel by a Sail Admin on the 'Lead Time & Grace Period Settings' screen). With the switch off the request is refused with "Office work-order generation is not enabled for this vessel."
- On the SHIP instance: no switch and no role check; the two job conditions below still apply.
- On both instances the job must be active.
- On both instances the job must not already have an active work order.
Steps:
1. Open 'Components' (Office: select the vessel first) and open the component in the component tree.
2. In Part C ('C. Jobs') the component's jobs are listed with Task Type, Frequency, Last Done Date and Next Due Date.
3. Click 'Generate WO' in the Actions column of the job's row.
4. In the 'Generate Work Order' pop-up choose the reason: 'Planning - Scheduled ahead of time', 'Breakdown - Emergency repair needed' or 'Other - Custom reason'.
5. The work order is generated and appears on the Work Orders screen.
Exceptions / edge cases:
- Duplicate: if the job already has an active work order, the system refuses to generate another.
- Inactive job: refused with "Cannot generate work orders for an inactive job".
- The Sail Admin requirement of the office 'Generate Now' button does NOT apply here; the two buttons use different server checks. See office-generate-now.md.
Where the manual differs:
- The June manuals present 'Generate WO' as unconditional. On the office instance the vessel switch must be on. Recorded in CONFLICTS.md.
Related procedures: planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md · office-generate-now.md · unplanned-wo.md
